ingredients.title: For the chicken salad
items: (2) 5 oz cans of chicken, drained (I like Wild Planet) or 1 heaping cup rotisserie chicken, chopped
Heaping 1/4 cup of dill from 1 small bunch
2 small scallions, dark and light green parts only
3 heaping teaspoons dill or sweet relish
A ton of freshly ground black peppercorns
A few drops of your favorite hot sauce, optional (I like Crystal and green Tabasco)

ingredients.title: For the toast
items: Crusty bread, like sourdough or country bread, or a fluffy Japanese milk bread/Brioche for a soft sandwich
2-3 tablespoons butter or olive oil, for the skillet

ingredients.title: For serving
items: Flaky salt and freshly ground black peppercorns

steps: Start by dicing both of the Persian cucumbers as small as you can comfortably get them, then add to a colander with a big pinch of kosher salt to drain, occasionally giving the colander a shake right up until you’re ready to combine with the chicken salad and serve.
Drain your canned chicken or chop a heaping cup of rotisserie chicken and add to a large mixing bowl.

Roughly chop about 1/4 cup of dill and thinly slice the dark and light green parts of 2 small scallions. Add the bulbs/white parts of the scallions to water to regrow or use for another purpose :-) Roughly chop 3 tablespoons pepperoncini, 8 cornichons, and 1 heaping tablespoon drained capers. Add everything to the mixing bowl along with the teaspoon of pickle juice.

Add the rest of your ingredients to the bowl: 3 teaspoons relish, 3 teaspoons whole-grain mustard, 1/3 cup + 2 tablespoons mayo, juice of half a lemon, 1 teaspoon champagne vinegar, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, lots of freshly ground black pepper, a few drops of your favorite hot sauce, 2 teaspoons of olive oil, and use a fork to mash the chicken down into the bowl. Fold everything together until nicely combined, finally adding the cucumbers and mixing them in when you’re ready to serve.

To make your toast, add a couple of tablespoons of butter or olive oil to a large cast iron over medium heat, once warmed through, 4 minutes, add the bread to the pan and add pressure to the top to get it nice and crispy (I use a grill press here but you can also press down with a spatula). Griddle for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown, then remove to a plate. Alternatively, use milk bread/Brioche to make a sandwich.
Top the toast with the chicken salad, more dill, a pinch of sumac, and serve alongside a large handful of dill pickle flavored-chips and some more cornichons. Enjoy!
